chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Abdullah, Sahib Al Sayyari, regarding what I know, or someone else, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him).

He said: Regarding what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Musa (peace be upon him): 'O Musa! Thank Me as is the right of thanking Me.' So he said: 'O Lord! And how can I thank You as is the right of Your thanking, and there is no thanks with which I thank You except that You have favored with it upon me?' He said: 'O Musa! Now you have thanked Me, when you knew that that is from Me.'

key_terms.حَقَّ شُكْرِي: The right/proper manner of thanking Me
key_terms.صَاحِبِ السَّابِرِيِّ: The companion of As-Sabiri (a title for Abu Abdullah)

ai.seo_question: What is the true meaning of thanking God according to the revelation to Musa?
ai.summary: This hadith, recorded in al-Kafi, elucidates the Shia theological concept that true gratitude (shukr) is not merely performing acts of worship, but the intellectual recognition that the very ability to be grateful is itself a divine gift. The dialogue highlights the infinite nature of God's favors, where the acknowledgment of the source of one's capacity for thankfulness constitutes the highest form of worship. This narrative reinforces the principle that self-awareness of divine grace is the foundation of spiritual contentment.
